key_insight: Cold welding and over-welding are the two most dangerous hidden defects in PE pipe butt fusion joints because they alter interfacial molecular entanglement and thermal degradation, leading to brittle long-term failure.
engineering_relevance: The review links welding-process deviations to joint structure, mechanical durability, and microwave sensing signals, offering a pathway for more reliable pipeline quality control.
method: Compare defect formation under low vs excessive heat input
Trace structure–property–signal pathway from microstructure to microwave S-parameters
Assess conventional NDT, ultrasonics, and MNDT for defect detection
evidence_signal: The abstract synthesizes reported relationships between defect severity and changes in tensile performance, slow crack growth resistance, permittivity, |S11|, |S21|, phase shift, resonance, and Q-factor rather than presenting new experimental data.
watch_item: Engineering adoption still depends on benchmark datasets, quantitative inversion, lift-off robustness, and standards for reliable microwave-based inspection.
paper_title: Cold-Welding and Over-Welding in Polyethylene Pipe Butt Fusion Joints: Formation Mechanisms, Structure–Property Degradation, and Emerging Microwave-Based Detection Strategies
